features.note: OPEN shot: two dark-gray vertical strips present at the front opening at approximately the correct ±x positions and correct height. However they read as frame elements, not as distinct EIA mounting rails — no U-hole or notch meso-pattern, no 44.45 mm pitch rhythm, and rear rails are not discernible behind the interior white wall. Front strip geometry is present but under-differentiated from the corner posts.

MESH shot: dark door panel shows a clear regular fine-dot perforation field across the full face — does NOT read as a solid panel. Open-area texture is legible and immediately recognizable as perforated mesh. Hinge seam visible on the left edge.

GLASS shot: door reads as transmissive/translucent (interior white wall faintly visible behind, lighter center vs. side panel). Blue LED edge-strip runs as a clean glowing blue line along the top, left, and bottom frame perimeter — the Panduit-aisle identity cue is unmistakable. Strong blockout delivery of the emissive feature.

Both MESH and GLASS shots: distinct black rectangular protrusion at the right (leading) edge of the door face. Reads as a graspable handle, not a decal. Shape is boxy/rectangular rather than a true lever profile, but adequate at blockout resolution.

important_features.note: Tall narrow cabinet (~3:1 H:W pixel ratio) consistent with 2.00 m H / 0.60 m W spec. Top cap distinctly visible. Base plinth present and flush to the ground plane — not floating. No casters or levelers visible; the plinth base is a flat solid. Silhouette reads correctly as a freestanding aisle-facing server cabinet despite missing casters.

defects: D1 [critical blocker]: Rails not visually differentiated from frame posts — two dark front strips at ±x are present but have no U-hole, notch, or pitch pattern; they read as inner frame members, not EIA 19" mounting rails.

D2 [critical blocker]: Rear mounting rails absent or completely occluded — OPEN shot shows only the interior white wall behind the front strips; no rear rail geometry is discernible at this camera angle.
D3: Casters/levelers absent — plinth bottom is a flat solid, no wheel or pad geometry present.
D4: Glass door transmissivity very subtle — interior faintly visible but nearly opaque; rails will not show through the closed glass door at voxel pass unless opacity/roughness is reduced.
D5: Lever handle reads as a rectangular pull block, not a lever profile — minor at blockout, flag for voxel pass.
corrections: Add a U-pattern visual cue to the front mounting rails: at minimum a distinct dark/light rhythm at ~44 mm pitch along each strip (alpha-mapped slot row, or spaced notch geometry) so the strips unambiguously read as rack rails rather than cabinet frame posts.
Ensure rear mounting rails exist as distinct geometry at x=±0.232 and are at least partially visible through the open door at this camera angle (42° azimuth, 18° elevation).
Add 4 caster/wheel cylinders (~0.04 m diameter) under the plinth corners to complete the floor-standing silhouette.
Reduce glass door opacity (increase transmission) so the rail geometry behind it is visible through the closed glass variant — prepare for voxel pass where this see-through cue is identity-defining.
